chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

A slave of his came to him, so he said to him: 'Have you spent anything today?' He said, 'No, by Allah.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'From where will Allah replace upon us? Spend, and even if it is one dirham.'

key_terms.أَنْفَقْتَ: You spent (from the root nafaqa, indicating expenditure in the way of God or general spending)
key_terms.دِرْهَماً: A dirham, a unit of currency
key_terms.مَوْلًى: A slave or freed slave under one's guardianship
key_terms.يُخْلِفُ: He will replace (referring to divine compensation for what is spent)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and economic benefit of spending money according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) instructs his slave to spend even a single dirham, emphasizing that Allah’s promise of replacement (*kaffarah*) is contingent upon the act of giving itself. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the immediacy of divine recompense for expenditure, encouraging believers to overcome stinginess by trusting in God’s sufficiency rather than hoarding wealth. The narration underscores that the spiritual benefit and material return are linked directly to the willingness to part with one’s possessions, no matter how small.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A slave of his<sup>asws</sup> came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Have you spent anything today?’ He said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So from where will Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Replace upon us? Spend, and even though it is one Dirham’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah in a marfu‘ manner from who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah or abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘Allah sends help from Heaven equal to the amount of expenditure. When one is certain about (Allah’s) replacing what is spent, his soul allows him to spend generously.”
